title: LiteRT Quantization, Delegates, and Benchmarking Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies litert quantization, delegates, and benchmarking?
options: Benchmark end to end and per stage, verify accuracy and delegate coverage, and select by representative evidence with safe fallback.
questions.answer: Benchmark end to end and per stage, verify accuracy and delegate coverage, and select by representative evidence with safe fallback.
questions.explanation: The correct response preserves authority, compatibility, exact artifact evidence, adverse-path behavior, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: A delegate either executes the entire LiteRT graph or cannot be used at all.
questions.explanation: Reporting only warm delegate inference time hides model download, initialization, preprocessing, fallback, and first-run cost users experience.

questions.prompt: Why can delegate partitioning make inference slower?
questions.answer: Unsupported operations force backend boundaries and synchronization or data-transfer overhead that can exceed accelerated gains.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the contract or mechanism that remains valid beyond one implementation demonstration.
